answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence decays when paths must cross a narrow boundary. A sybil garden may contain many mutually endorsing nodes, yet a sparse external cut gives it low conductance: few walk transitions reach honest nodes. Under bounded-degree and mixing assumptions, min-cut and transitivity bounds cap its reachable trust and aggregate voting weight by boundary connectivity, not headcount; coloring the cluster with one pigment cannot lift that nadir.
